decisions.reason: The candidate already covers invalid-code mints and random allocation to an existing NFT holder; the source only refines the feedback wording.
The invalid-code feedback wording does not affect badge content or layout; the badge clause in the same message is a separate decision already represented.
The referral-feedback wording change does not alter NFT cover sizing or visibility; the NFT-size clause is separate runtime evidence.
The source Event changes referral-feedback copy, not the View Book action, label, or visibility rule.
The client requests an exact invalid-code popup wording change but does not request a corresponding FAQ revision.
The source state before and after preserves the same no-or-invalid-code $5 allocation meaning; the Event only changes the popup sentence from shorthand to 'will go'.
The source concerns feedback for blank or invalid codes and does not change commission behavior for a successful mint using a valid referral code.
Mentioning a $500 prize-draw ticket in feedback copy does not change the Small Block prize amount, trigger, eligibility, or draw mechanics.
The source requests a popup wording adjustment and contains no instruction to revise the About page.
The source addresses blank-or-invalid-code allocation feedback, not ticket issuance to a referrer's NFT after a valid code-used mint.
The wording change does not alter ticket counters, dashboard ticket display, or accounting behavior.
The invalid-code feedback wording does not change how referral codes are derived, displayed, shared, or retained.
